title: Bathroom Break
can_do: 需要上厕所时，立即让成人暂停活动，并在回来后按自己的准备情况继续。

conversation_move.label: request a pause for a body need

trigger: While Dad prepares another round of the tabletop game, Child notices he needs the bathroom and interrupts.
core_response: I need to use the bathroom.
repair_response: Wait, I need to go now.
setting: A tabletop animal-card game at home, paused for a bathroom break and resumed only after a later return.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: I need to use the bathroom.

turns.speaker: dad
turns.line: Welcome back. Your card's still here.

turns.speaker: dad
turns.line: Go ahead. Put your card here.

replay_cards.title: A rest during dancing
replay_cards.setting: Dancing together in the living room
replay_cards.change: He feels tired and wants a rest while Dad is about to start another song
replay_cards.challenge: Tell Dad he needs to rest. Dad stops the music immediately and helps him settle. Only after resting, if Dad offers to restart, he may say 'I'm not ready yet. Can I have two more minutes?' Dad accepts the need for more rest; he can later choose to continue or finish. Extra speech is optional and no restart is required.

replay_cards.title: Bathroom before leaving
replay_cards.setting: At the front door before going out
replay_cards.change: He notices a bathroom need after putting his shoes on
replay_cards.challenge: Tell Dad now. If Dad did not hear the first signal, clarify 'Wait, I need to go now.' Dad stops departure as soon as he hears, accompanies him as needed, and leaves the outing preparations in place. No shoe task or extra English line comes before care.

parent_support: Stop the game and make departure possible at the first bathroom signal, in any language or gesture. Never ask whether to pause or require more English before he can go.
Keep his cards untouched and acknowledge his return promise while he is already leaving; the promise does not earn permission. Accompany him if he needs help without requiring another sentence.
Allow an ordinary bathroom break and handwashing off-screen. After he returns, ask whether he is ready; resume only if he wants to. Never rush the break to complete the scene.
This is a calm pretend scene. If a real bathroom need arises, stop the role-play immediately and help him; do not finish or repeat the script.
